plain: To openly condemn or speak against something.

webster.text: To cry down; to censure as faulty, mean or worthless; to clamor against; to discredit by finding fault; as, to decry a poem.

example.quote: If I see gentlemen pass by in silence such parts as they vehemently decry out of doors, or such
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 4, North Carolina Convention, Mr. MACLAINE, July 24, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
